# Shared Technical Standards

Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.

---

## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist

The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:

| Banned Feature | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
| `mask` | Masks |
| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
| `textPath` | Text along a path |
| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |

---

## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives

| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
|---------------|---------------------|
| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |

**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.

---

## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference

### Presentations

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |

### Social Media

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |

### Marketing Materials

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |

---

## 4. Basic SVG Rules

- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

---

## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)

Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

**Prohibited**:
- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`

**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.

---

## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques

> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).

### Shadow

#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended

Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
    <feMerge>
      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
    </feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
```

Recommended parameters:
```
stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
dx:             0–2
```

#### Colored Shadow

Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.

```xml
<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
  <feMerge>
    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
  </feMerge>
</filter>
```

Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.

#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback

Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:

```xml
<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
<!-- Main card -->
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
```

### Image Overlay

#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common

Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).

```xml
<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
```

#### Bottom Gradient Bar

Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
```

#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect

Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.

```xml
<defs>
  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
  </radialGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
```

#### Brand Color Overlay

Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
```

### Quick-Reference Table

| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
|----------|-----------------------|-------|
| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |

---

## 7. Project Directory Structure

```
project/
├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
```

75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)
84	
85	Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:
86	
87	```bash
88	# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
89	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
90	
91	# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
92	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
93	
94	# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
95	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
96	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
97	```
98	
99	**Prohibited**:
100	- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
101	- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
102	- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`
103	
104	**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
109	
110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
111	
112	### Shadow
113	
114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
115	
116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
117	
118	```xml
119	<defs>
120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
125	    <feMerge>
126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
128	    </feMerge>
129	  </filter>
130	</defs>
131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
132	```
133	
134	Recommended parameters:
135	```
136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
139	dx:             0–2
140	```
141	
142	#### Colored Shadow
143	
144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
145	
146	```xml
147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
152	  <feMerge>
153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
155	  </feMerge>
156	</filter>
157	```
158	
159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
160	
161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
162	
163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
164	
165	```xml
166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
170	<!-- Main card -->
171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
172	```
173	
174	### Image Overlay
175	
176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
177	
178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
179	
180	```xml
181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
182	<defs>
183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
187	  </linearGradient>
188	</defs>
189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
190	```
191	
192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
193	
194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
195	
196	```xml
197	<defs>
198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
201	  </linearGradient>
202	</defs>
203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
204	```
205	
206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
207	
208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
209	
210	```xml
211	<defs>
212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
215	  </radialGradient>
216	</defs>
217	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
218	```
219	
220	#### Brand Color Overlay
221	
222	Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.
223	
224	```xml
225	<defs>
226	  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
227	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
228	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
229	  </linearGradient>
230	</defs>
231	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
232	```
233	
234	### Quick-Reference Table
235	
236	| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
237	|----------|-----------------------|-------|
238	| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
239	| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
240	| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
241	| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
242	| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
243	| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |
244	
245	---
246

250	project/
251	├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)

258	```

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#0D1B2A"/>
  <rect x="80" y="60" width="900" height="60" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="8"/>
  <text x="100" y="102" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="28" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold">Closed-Loop Pipeline: From Multi-User Interaction to Shared Skill Evolution</text>
  <text x="1180" y="102" fill="#4ECDC4" font-size="14" font-family="Arial" text-anchor="end">3 / 8</text>

  <!-- Central circular loop diagram -->
  <circle cx="640" cy="380" r="200" fill="none" stroke="#1B3A5A" stroke-width="40"/>
  <circle cx="640" cy="380" r="200" fill="none" stroke="#00D4C8" stroke-width="40" stroke-dasharray="314" stroke-dashoffset="0" stroke-linecap="round"/>

  <!-- Four stage labels around the circle -->
  <g font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold">
    <text x="640" y="130" fill="#00D4C8" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle">Evidence</text>
    <text x="840" y="320" fill="#FFD93D" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle">Attribution</text>
    <text x="640" y="570" fill="#4ECDC4" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle">Evolution</text>
    <text x="440" y="320" fill="#00D4C8" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle">Distribution</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Stage descriptions -->
  <g font-family="Arial" font-size="12" fill="#B8C5D0">
    <text x="640" y="155" text-anchor="middle">Analyze trajectories</text>
    <text x="870" y="380" text-anchor="middle">Diagnose root</text>
    <text x="870" y="395" text-anchor="middle">causes</text>
    <text x="640" y="600" text-anchor="middle">Propose skill</text>
    <text x="640" y="615" text-anchor="middle">mutations</text>
    <text x="410" y="380" text-anchor="middle">Sync to all</text>
    <text x="410" y="395" text-anchor="middle">agents</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Multi-user input -->
  <rect x="100" y="320" width="180" height="120" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="10"/>
  <text x="190" y="355" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="16" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Multi-User</text>
  <text x="190" y="375" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="16" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Interaction</text>
  <g fill="#B8C5D0" font-size="11" font-family="Arial" text-anchor="middle">
    <text x="190" y="400">OpenClaw, CoPaw, IronClaw,</text>
    <text x="190" y="415">PicoClaw, ZeroClaw, NanoClaw</text>
  </g>
  <path d="M280 380 L390 380" stroke="#00D4C8" stroke-width="3" fill="none" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>

  <!-- Session Collection -->
  <rect x="980" y="320" width="180" height="120" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="10"/>
  <text x="1070" y="355" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="16" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Skill</text>
  <text x="1070" y="375" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="16" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Synchronization</text>
  <g fill="#B8C5D0" font-size="11" font-family="Arial" text-anchor="middle">
    <text x="1070" y="400">Updated skills</text>
    <text x="1070" y="415">→ all agents</text>
  </g>
  <path d="M890 380 L980 380" stroke="#4ECDC4" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/>

  <!-- Closed loop arrows -->
  <path d="M640 180 A200 200 0 0 1 840 380" stroke="#00D4C8" stroke-width="3" fill="none" stroke-dasharray="8,4"/>
  <path d="M840 380 A200 200 0 0 1 640 580" stroke="#FFD93D" stroke-width="3" fill="none" stroke-dasharray="8,4"/>
  <path d="M640 580 A200 200 0 0 1 440 380" stroke="#4ECDC4" stroke-width="3" fill="none" stroke-dasharray="8,4"/>
  <path d="M440 380 A200 200 0 0 1 640 180" stroke="#00D4C8" stroke-width="3" fill="none" stroke-dasharray="8,4"/>

  <text x="640" y="380" fill="#0D1B2A" font-size="14" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">CLOSED</text>
  <text x="640" y="395" fill="#0D1B2A" font-size="14" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">LOOP</text>

  <!-- Legend -->
  <g transform="translate(100, 560)">
    <rect width="1080" height="80" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="8"/>
    <text x="20" y="30" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="14" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold">Key: Agentic evolver analyzes skill-specific groups through three open-ended reasoning stages</text>
    <circle cx="30" cy="55" r="8" fill="#00D4C8"/>
    <text x="50" y="60" fill="#B8C5D0" font-size="12" font-family="Arial">Evidence →</text>
    <circle cx="130" cy="55" r="8" fill="#FFD93D"/>
    <text x="150" y="60" fill="#B8C5D0" font-size="12" font-family="Arial">Attribution →</text>
    <circle cx="240" cy="55" r="8" fill="#4ECDC4"/>
    <text x="260" y="60" fill="#B8C5D0" font-size="12" font-family="Arial">Evolution →</text>
    <circle cx="350" cy="55" r="8" fill="#00D4C8"/>
    <text x="370" y="60" fill="#B8C5D0" font-size="12" font-family="Arial">Distribution</text>
  </g>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#0D1B2A"/>
  <rect x="80" y="60" width="900" height="60" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="8"/>
  <text x="100" y="102" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="28" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold">Agentic Evolver: Evidence → Attribution → Evolution</text>
  <text x="1180" y="102" fill="#4ECDC4" font-size="14" font-family="Arial" text-anchor="end">4 / 8</text>

  <!-- Three stage pipeline -->
  <!-- Stage 1: Evidence -->
  <rect x="80" y="180" width="340" height="400" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="80" y="180" width="340" height="60" fill="#00D4C8" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="80" y="210" width="340" height="30" fill="#00D4C8"/>
  <text x="250" y="222" fill="#0D1B2A" font-size="20" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">1. Evidence</text>
  <g fill="#B8C5D0" font-family="Arial" font-size="15">
    <text x="100" y="270">Analyze trajectories to identify</text>
    <text x="100" y="295">behavioral patterns across</text>
    <text x="100" y="320">multi-user sessions</text>
    <text x="100" y="370">Input: Structured session</text>
    <text x="100" y="395">trajectories preserving</text>
    <text x="100" y="420">full action–feedback</text>
    <text x="100" y="445">causal chains</text>
  </g>
  <text x="100" y="560" fill="#FFD93D" font-size="13" font-family="Arial">Pattern detection from</text>
  <text x="100" y="578" fill="#FFD93D" font-size="13" font-family="Arial">diverse user contexts</text>

  <!-- Arrow 1 -->
  <polygon points="440,380 480,360 480,400" fill="#00D4C8"/>
  <line x1="420" y1="380" x2="475" y2="380" stroke="#00D4C8" stroke-width="3"/>

  <!-- Stage 2: Attribution -->
  <rect x="490" y="180" width="340" height="400" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="490" y="180" width="340" height="60" fill="#FFD93D" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="490" y="210" width="340" height="30" fill="#FFD93D"/>
  <text x="660" y="222" fill="#0D1B2A" font-size="20" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2. Attribution</text>
  <g fill="#B8C5D0" font-family="Arial" font-size="15">
    <text x="510" y="270">Diagnose root causes of</text>
    <text x="510" y="295">failures and successes</text>
    <text x="510" y="320">to understand why skills</text>
    <text x="510" y="345">work or break</text>
    <text x="510" y="395">Identifies: Generalizable</text>
    <text x="510" y="420">improvements vs.</text>
    <text x="510" y="445">idiosyncratic fixes</text>
  </g>
  <text x="510" y="560" fill="#FF6B6B" font-size="13" font-family="Arial">Single user rarely generates</text>
  <text x="510" y="578" fill="#FF6B6B" font-size="13" font-family="Arial">enough signal alone</text>

  <!-- Arrow 2 -->
  <polygon points="850,380 890,360 890,400" fill="#FFD93D"/>
  <line x1="830" y1="380" x2="885" y2="380" stroke="#FFD93D" stroke-width="3"/>

  <!-- Stage 3: Evolution -->
  <rect x="900" y="180" width="300" height="400" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="900" y="180" width="300" height="60" fill="#4ECDC4" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="900" y="210" width="300" height="30" fill="#4ECDC4"/>
  <text x="1050" y="222" fill="#0D1B2A" font-size="20" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">3. Evolution</text>
  <g fill="#B8C5D0" font-family="Arial" font-size="15">
    <text x="920" y="270">Propose skill mutations</text>
    <text x="920" y="295">— refine existing or</text>
    <text x="920" y="320">create new skills</text>
    <text x="920" y="370">Open-ended agent</text>
    <text x="920" y="395">reasoning over</text>
    <text x="920" y="420">evidence</text>
    <text x="920" y="460">NOT predefined rules</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Key insight box -->
  <rect x="80" y="620" width="1120" height="60" fill="#0D1B2A" stroke="#00D4C8" stroke-width="2" rx="8"/>
  <text x="640" y="655" fill="#00D4C8" font-size="16" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">KEY: Agentic evolver drives skill updates through autonomous reasoning, not rule-based logic</text>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#0D1B2A"/>
  <rect x="80" y="60" width="900" height="60" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="8"/>
  <text x="100" y="102" fill="#FFFFFF" font-size="28" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold">Key Takeaways: Three Properties That Distinguish SkillClaw</text>
  <text x="1180" y="102" fill="#4ECDC4" font-size="14" font-family="Arial" text-anchor="end">8 / 8</text>

  <!-- Three pillars -->
  <!-- Pillar 1 -->
  <rect x="80" y="160" width="360" height="320" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="80" y="160" width="360" height="80" fill="#00D4C8" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="80" y="200" width="360" height="40" fill="#00D4C8"/>
  <text x="260" y="212" fill="#0D1B2A" font-size="18" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">1. Collective Evolution</text>
  <g fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial" font-size="15">
    <text x="110" y="280">Knowledge from individual</text>
    <text x="110" y="310">interactions contributes to</text>
    <text x="110" y="340">a shared, continuously</text>
    <text x="110" y="370">improving skill ecosystem</text>
  </g>
  <text x="110" y="440" fill="#B8C5D0" font-size="13" font-family="Arial">Multi-user trajectories →</text>
  <text x="110" y="460" fill="#B8C5D0" font-size="13" font-family="Arial">shared improvement</text>

  <!-- Pillar 2 -->
  <rect x="460" y="160" width="360" height="320" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="460" y="160" width="360" height="80" fill="#FFD93D" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="460" y="200" width="360" height="40" fill="#FFD93D"/>
  <text x="640" y="212" fill="#0D1B2A" font-size="18" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2. Fully Automatic</text>
  <g fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial" font-size="15">
    <text x="490" y="280">Skill evolution driven by</text>
    <text x="490" y="310">runtime interaction without</text>
    <text x="490" y="340">manual curation or explicit</text>
    <text x="490" y="370">user intervention</text>
  </g>
  <text x="490" y="440" fill="#B8C5D0" font-size="13" font-family="Arial">No human in the loop</text>

  <!-- Pillar 3 -->
  <rect x="840" y="160" width="360" height="320" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="840" y="160" width="360" height="80" fill="#4ECDC4" rx="12"/>
  <rect x="840" y="200" width="360" height="40" fill="#4ECDC4"/>
  <text x="1020" y="212" fill="#0D1B2A" font-size="18" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">3. Agentic Evolution</text>
  <g fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial" font-size="15">
    <text x="870" y="280">Skill updates produced</text>
    <text x="870" y="310">through open-ended</text>
    <text x="870" y="340">reasoning rather than</text>
    <text x="870" y="370">predefined update rules</text>
  </g>
  <text x="870" y="440" fill="#B8C5D0" font-size="13" font-family="Arial">Autonomous agent reasoning</text>

  <!-- Implications box -->
  <rect x="80" y="510" width="1120" height="100" fill="#1B3A5A" rx="8"/>
  <text x="100" y="545" fill="#FFD93D" font-size="18" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold">Implications for Building Continuously Improving Agent Systems</text>
  <g fill="#B8C5D0" font-family="Arial" font-size="15">
    <text x="100" y="580">SkillClaw compatible with OpenClaw, CoPaw, IronClaw, PicoClaw, ZeroClaw, NanoClaw, NemoClaw</text>
    <text x="100" y="605">Evaluated on WildClawBench using Qwen3-Max — substantial improvements across tasks</text>
  </g>

  <text x="1260" y="700" fill="#4ECDC4" font-size="12" font-family="Arial" text-anchor="end">arxiv.org/abs/2604.08377</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# SkillClaw Presentation — Speaker Notes

---

# 01_title

SkillClaw enables LLM agent skills to continuously evolve by aggregating cross-user interaction trajectories and applying agentic, evidence-driven skill updates. Today we'll explore how this framework closes the loop between individual user interactions and collective skill improvement.

**Key points**: (1) Title establishes the core contribution (2) Collective evolution is the key differentiator (3) Agentic evolver enables autonomous skill improvement

**Duration**: 1 minute

---

# 02_problem

[Transition] To understand why SkillClaw matters, we first need to recognize the fundamental limitation of current LLM agent systems.

Current LLM agents like OpenClaw rely on reusable skills, but these skills remain static after deployment. Users manually install skills from a centralized hub, and solutions discovered during interaction rarely persist beyond individual sessions. As similar tasks recur across different users over time, the same patterns of failure and recovery are repeatedly observed, yet the system does not improve.

Memory-based approaches store past trajectories but remain tied to specific instances and are hard to generalize. Skill-based methods compress experience into structured instructions but treat the resulting library as a static resource that does not evolve through usage.

**Key points**: (1) Skills are static post-deployment (2) Failures are rediscovered independently (3) No system-level knowledge accumulation

**Duration**: 2 minutes

---

# 03_architecture

[Transition] SkillClaw addresses this through a closed-loop pipeline that transforms multi-user interactions into shared skill improvements.

The framework adopts a centralized evolution architecture with four stages: Multi-user interaction feeds into session collection, which triggers the agentic evolver, whose outputs are synchronized back to all agents.

The agentic evolver analyzes each skill-specific group through three stages: Evidence analysis identifies behavioral patterns, Attribution diagnoses root causes of failures and successes, and Evolution proposes skill mutations — refining existing skills or creating new ones.

Updated skills are verified before being merged into the shared repository and synchronized back to all agents. The process is driven by autonomous agent reasoning over interaction evidence, not predefined update rules.

**Key points**: (1) Four-stage closed loop (2) Agentic evolver core (3) No predefined rules — open-ended reasoning

**Duration**: 2 minutes

---

# 04_evolver

[Transition] Let's look deeper at how the agentic evolver actually works.

The evolver processes trajectories through three sequential stages. In the Evidence stage, it analyzes trajectories to identify behavioral patterns across multi-user sessions. Input consists of structured session trajectories preserving full action–feedback causal chains.

In Attribution, it diagnoses root causes of failures and successes to understand why skills work or break. This stage identifies which improvements are generalizable versus which are idiosyncratic fixes — a critical distinction.

In Evolution, it proposes skill mutations through open-ended agent reasoning — not predefined rules. This can mean refining existing skills or creating new ones based on the accumulated evidence.

The critical insight: a single user rarely generates enough signal to separate generalizable improvements from idiosyncratic fixes. Cross-user aggregation is essential.

**Key points**: (1) Three-stage pipeline (2) Open-ended reasoning not rules (3) Cross-user signal aggregation essential

**Duration**: 2 minutes

---

# 05_aggregation

[Transition] This brings us to why cross-user trajectory aggregation is so powerful.

SkillClaw is compatible with a range of Claw-style agent systems: OpenClaw, CoPaw, IronClaw, PicoClaw, ZeroClaw, NanoClaw, and NemoClaw. Each exercises the same skills under diverse contexts.

When trajectories from different users are aggregated and grouped by referenced skills, they form a shared evidence base. Different users exercising the same skill under diverse contexts produce complementary views of that skill's behavioral boundary — revealing both conditions under which it works and those under which it breaks.

This cross-user aggregation exposes skill behavioral boundaries that no single user could discover alone. Success patterns and failure modes from multiple contexts combine to form a complete picture.

**Key points**: (1) Multiple Claw systems compatible (2) Complementary signals from diverse contexts (3) Single user cannot separate generalizable from idiosyncratic

**Duration**: 2 minutes

---

# 06_case_creative

[Transition] Now let's examine concrete evolution case studies. First, the multimodal creative task pipeline.

Over 6 days, 6 evolution candidates were proposed for the multimodal creative pipeline skill. Only 1 was accepted. Day 1 candidate — validate-tmp-workspace-inputs — was accepted and upgraded to the new best pool.

Days 2 through 6 were all rejected: multimodal-input-validation-and-setup, multimodal-creative-task-pipeline, two improved versions of the pipeline, and finally an extended PDF-to-poster candidate. Each time, the validator kept the current best pool.

This demonstrates the conservative verification process that prevents regressions. Only candidates that demonstrably improve without risk are accepted. The strict 1-of-6 acceptance rate reflects the high bar for safety.

**Key points**: (1) 1 of 6 accepted (2) Conservative verification (3) Prevents regressions

**Duration**: 2 minutes

---

# 07_case_git

[Transition] In contrast, let's look at the git push auth-fallback skill evolution.

Over 6 days, 3 of 6 candidates were accepted — a very different pattern. Day 1: git-push-with-auth-fallback was accepted for the safety best pool. Day 2: an improved version with unified patch/bundle filenames was accepted. Day 3: git-push-with-auth-fallback plus git-clone-to-directory was accepted with auth-alternative paths and secrets audit.

Day 4 had no new candidate — the validator confirmed the current pool as best and continued with it. Days 5 and 6 were rejected: attempts to add push hang handling and identity config improvements showed no improvement.

This demonstrates successful iterative refinement when evidence supports it. The skill was improved 3 times before reaching a plateau where further changes showed no benefit.

**Key points**: (1) 3 of 6 accepted (2) Successful iterative refinement (3) Plateau reached when evidence doesn't support further change

**Duration**: 2 minutes

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] To conclude, let's summarize the three properties that distinguish SkillClaw.

First: Collective evolution. Knowledge from individual interactions contributes to a shared, continuously improving skill ecosystem. Multi-user trajectories aggregate into shared improvement.

Second: Fully automatic. Skill evolution is driven by runtime interaction without manual curation or explicit user intervention. No human in the loop required.

Third: Agentic evolution paradigm. Skill updates are produced through open-ended reasoning rather than predefined update rules. The autonomous agent drives improvement.

For systems builders, SkillClaw is compatible with a range of Claw-style agent systems and has been evaluated on WildClawBench using Qwen3-Max, demonstrating substantial improvements across tasks.

**Key points**: (1) Three distinguishing properties (2) Collective, automatic, agentic (3) Proven on WildClawBench

**Duration**: 1 minute
